thread:
anya (CS): Hey team — following yesterday's paging window, I put together a short customer note + status page blurb. Need engineering sign-off on timeline and whether to offer a 10% SLA credit or 15% (customer is on dedicated plan).

incident-bot: Incident #2026-0423 assigned to @mike-oncall. Severity: SEV2. Page triggered at 2026-04-23T02:14Z.

mike-oncall: TL;DR: routing compile backlog + autoscaler rebalance caused transient 503s for some Dedicated pools. We mitigated by draining a misbehaving host group and rolling its allocation, traffic routed to fallback model variant during window. No data loss.

anya (CS): Proposed status page update (short):
```
Summary: Intermittent 503 errors affecting a subset of Dedicated inference pools. Impact: request failures and increased latency for some customers for ~22 minutes between 02:14–02:36 UTC.
Current status: Mitigated, stable. Root cause investigation ongoing.
Action: We rerouted traffic to fallback variants and replaced a misconfigured host group.
```

tim-engineering: Thanks. Timeline is mostly correct, but add the exact mitigation step time and the fallback start time. Fallback started at 02:18Z, host drain completed 02:32Z.

anya (CS): Updated blurb with times. Draft customer email below — short and apologetic, plus next steps. Please suggest edits.

anya (CS): Draft customer email:
"Hi <Customer>,

We experienced intermittent 503 errors impacting some Dedicated inference pools on 2026-04-23 between 02:14–02:36 UTC. We rerouted traffic to fallback model variants at 02:18 UTC and completed a controlled host group drain and replacement at 02:32 UTC. We are sorry for the disruption.

Our preliminary analysis shows the root cause is a routing compile backlog combined with an autoscaler rebalance that overloaded a small set of hosts. We are continuing a deeper RCA and will share final findings and preventive actions by 2026-04-28.

As a gesture of goodwill we propose a one-time SLA credit of 10% to the affected billing period. If you prefer 15% please let us know and we can escalate.

Sincerely,
The Redwood Inference Team"

alice-eng-sre: +1 on times. For the customer email I'd avoid 'we are sorry for the disruption' — keep it professional: 'We apologize for the disruption and the impact to your service.' Also confirm the affected model variant names? We should avoid noisy technical detail; say 'a small number of Dedicated hosts' rather than variant names.

mike-oncall: Confirming no user data was exposed or lost. We ran KV cache integrity checks and request replay showed only failed responses, not incorrect outputs.

sara-ops: Action items for post-incident:
- (ENG) Add compile backpressure circuit to routing compile step by 2026-04-28 (owner: @tim-engineering)
- (SRE) Improve autoscaler pre-checks to avoid draining simultaneous host groups by 2026-05-05 (owner: @alice-eng-sre)
- (CS) Finalize customer email and send by 2026-04-24 (owner: @anya (CS))
- (CS/Account) Check with account team whether customer expects 15% credit (owner: @kevin (Sales))

kevin (Sales): I'll ping the account lead and get back within 2 hours. If they want escalation, we can offer 15%.

tim-engineering: Quick note on root cause hypothesis: the routing compile queue spiked because a large batch of model warmups coincided with autoscaler churn. Need to throttle compile jobs and add higher priority for live traffic compiles. I'll scope a patch and timeline in the daily engineering sync.

anya (CS): Thanks. Can someone approve the final customer email wording? If I don't hear objections in 60m I'll send the email with the 10% credit offer and status page update.

alice-eng-sre: Approve.

mike-oncall: Approve.

kevin (Sales): Approve pending account confirmation (will update).

anya (CS): Sending out now. Posting final status page update and scheduling follow-up RCA sync for 2026-04-26 15:00 UTC. Will attach postmortem draft after that meeting. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-0423 (public)

anya (CS): Thanks everyone — will circle back with the RCA and preventative plan. If you want edits to the public text, @tim-engineering or @alice-eng-sre, DM me now.

mike-oncall: One last note — recommend flagging any similar Dedicated pools with version tags so routing analytics can alert earlier. Adding to action items.

sara-ops: Noted. Added to the ops tracker.

anya (CS): End of thread.
